The catch

Keeping 3 keys makes the final sum smaller, but this naïve selector still computed all 12 scores. Real speedups need a cheaper way to choose candidates.

A practical sparse system may use a local window, a router, or a compressed index to propose candidates. That saves work only if the proposal step is cheaper—and it can miss a useful key.
